contentObjective: I can compare ratios by finding unit rates or using equivalent ratios.
languageObjective: I can explain my comparison using the words unit rate, equivalent ratio, compare, and common denominator.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Decidir cuál razón es mayor, menor o igual usando razones equivalentes o tasas unitarias.
vocabulary.cloze: Make the ___ match, or find each ___ ___, before deciding which ratio is greater.

examples.why: Both reduced to the same unit.
Different quantities, so the totals say nothing.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the amount for exactly one unit, like 5 miles per 1 hour, is a ___.

examples.why: The amount for exactly one unit.
A rate for three, not one.

vocabulary.definition: Two ratios that mean the same thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos razones que significan lo mismo.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con números más pequeños que compara igual. 6:8 y 3:4 son la misma razón.

vocabulary.definition: A bottom number that two fractions can share so you can compare them.

vocabulary.visual: To compare 3/5 and 4/7, use LCD 35: 21/35 vs 20/35
vocabulary.cloze: A denominator shared by two fractions so they can be compared is a ___.

24 is a common multiple, but 12 is smaller.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad compartida a la que escalas ambas opciones para poder compararlas.

Two ratios that mean the same thing

steps: 1. Convert each ratio to a unit rate (e.g. price per item or miles per gallon)
2. Alternatively, scale both ratios to a common term (like a common denominator)
3. Compare the resulting unit rates to identify the better buy or faster rate

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Babysitting Pay
revealWordProblem.text:
Claire, Yuzuki, and Nakai compared the hours they babysat last weekend and what they were paid, shown on the calendar. A new family is looking for a babysitter and is offering $10.75 per hour.
Question: Who would want to take this offer, based on what they were paid the previous weekend?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Three calendar days showing each student's babysitting hours and pay: Claire 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. for $31.50, Yuzuki 12 p.m. to 8 p.m. for $63, Nakai 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. for $50.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each unit rate in dollars per hour. Claire worked 3 hours for $31.50, so $31.50 ÷ 3 = $10.50 per hour. Yuzuki worked 8 hours for $63, so $63 ÷ 8 = $7.875 per hour. Nakai worked 4 hours for $50, so $50 ÷ 4 = $12.50 per hour. The offer is $10.75 per hour. Claire ($10.50) and Yuzuki ($7.88) would both earn more than before, so they would want the offer. Nakai already earns $12.50 per hour, so the offer would be a pay cut for him.

questions.stem: Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
questions.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef A: 2÷8 = ___ cups per cracker.
The two ratios do not reduce to the same value, so they are not equal. Divide each cheese amount by its cracker count and compare the results.
You have both amounts, so a comparison is possible. Turn each ratio into cheese per cracker and the answer appears.
hints: You can't compare 2 cups and 3 cups directly — the chefs use different numbers of crackers.
Find each chef's cheese for ONE cracker: divide cheese by crackers for each, then compare the two rates.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compare those two decimals to see who uses more per cracker.
questions.stemEs: El chef A usa 2 tazas de queso por cada 8 galletas saladas. El chef B usa 3 tazas de queso por cada 9 galletas saladas. ¿Quién usa más queso por galleta?
questions.explanationEs: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 tazas por galleta. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 tazas por galleta. El chef B usa más queso por galleta.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 2 tazas y 3 tazas directamente: los chefs usan cantidades distintas de galletas.
Halla el queso de cada chef para UNA galleta: divide queso entre galletas en cada caso y luego compara las dos tasas.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compara esos dos decimales para ver quién usa más por galleta.

questions.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.
choiceFeedback: Compare the ratios carefully — which one is greater?
Rewrite both ratios with the same second number before deciding — scale the first ratio so its second term is 8, then compare.
Both ratios are exact numbers, so they can be compared. Scale one of them until the second terms match.
hints: The second numbers (4 and 8) don't match, so the ratios aren't ready to compare yet.
Rewrite the ratios with the same second number — 8 works nicely, since 4 × 2 = 8 — then compare the first numbers.
Scale 3:4 by 2: multiply both parts to get an out-of-8 ratio. Then compare its first number with the 5 in 5:8.
questions.explanationEs: Convierte a un denominador común: 3:4 = 6:8. Como 6:8 > 5:8, la razón 3:4 es mayor.
hintsEs: Los segundos números (4 y 8) no coinciden, así que las razones todavía no están listas para compararse.
Reescribe las razones con el mismo segundo número —el 8 funciona bien, porque 4 × 2 = 8— y luego compara los primeros números.
Escala 3:4 por 2: multiplica ambas partes para obtener una razón sobre 8. Luego compara su primer número con el 5 de 5:8.

questions.stem: Which lemonade recipe is more lemony? Recipe A: 2 lemons for 6 cups of water. Recipe B: 3 lemons for 7 cups of water.
questions.explanation: Recipe A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 lemons per cup. Recipe B: 3÷7 ≈ 0.43 lemons per cup. Since 0.43 > 0.33, Recipe B is more lemony.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Recipe A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 lemons per cup.
The ratios 2:6 and 3:7 do not reduce to the same value. Find the lemons per cup for each recipe and compare the decimals.
Every number you need is given. Divide lemons by cups for each recipe to compare them fairly.
hints: Recipe B has more lemons, but it also has more water — so compare rates, not raw counts.
Find lemons per ONE cup of water for each recipe: divide lemons by cups. The bigger rate is more lemony.
Recipe A: divide 2 ÷ 6. Recipe B: divide 3 ÷ 7. Compare the two decimals you get.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál receta de limonada tiene más sabor a limón? Receta A: 2 limones por 6 tazas de agua. Receta B: 3 limones por 7 tazas de agua.
questions.explanationEs: Receta A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 limones por taza. Receta B: 3÷7 ≈ 0.43 limones por taza. Como 0.43 > 0.33, la receta B tiene más sabor a limón.
hintsEs: La receta B tiene más limones, pero también más agua, así que compara tasas, no conteos sueltos.
Halla los limones por UNA taza de agua en cada receta: divide limones entre tazas. La tasa mayor sabe más a limón.
Receta A: divide 2 ÷ 6. Receta B: divide 3 ÷ 7. Compara los dos decimales que obtengas.

steps: 1. Convert each ratio to a unit rate (e.g. price per item or miles per gallon)
2. Alternatively, scale both ratios to a common term (like a common denominator)
3. Compare the resulting unit rates to identify the better buy or faster rate
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Compare Ratios is thinking the ratio with the bigger raw number automatically wins — like assuming Chef Tran's 8 tablespoons of cocoa must be more chocolatey than Chef Reyes's 6 tablespoons, without checking that the milk amounts (14 oz vs. 10 oz) are different. Never compare the raw numbers alone — always scale both ratios to the same amount or find each unit rate first.

level1.stem: Shop A sells 2 cookies for $4. Shop B sells 3 cookies for $9. What is the lower price for 1 cookie?
level1.stemEs: La tienda A vende 2 galletas por $4. La tienda B vende 3 galletas por $9. ¿Cuál es el precio más bajo por 1 galleta?
hints: Divide each cost by the number of cookies.
hintsEs: Divide cada costo entre el número de galletas.
level1.explanation: Find each price for 1 cookie: $4 ÷ 2 = $2; $9 ÷ 3 = $3 Choose the lower price: $2 < $3
level1.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 galleta: $4 ÷ 2 = $2; $9 ÷ 3 = $3 Elige el precio más bajo: $2 < $3

level1.stem: Drink A uses 1 cup of juice for 2 cups of water. Drink B uses 2 cups of juice for 3 cups of water. Scale both to 6 cups of water. Which drink has more juice?
level1.stemEs: La bebida A usa 1 taza de jugo por 2 tazas de agua. La bebida B usa 2 tazas de jugo por 3 tazas de agua. Escala las dos a 6 tazas de agua. ¿Qué bebida tiene más jugo?
hints: With the same water, the drink with more juice wins.
hintsEs: Con la misma agua, gana la bebida con más jugo.
level1.explanation: Scale both drinks to 6 cups: 1 × 3 = 3 → 3:6; 2 × 2 = 4 → 4:6 Compare the juice: 4 > 3
level1.explanationEs: Escala las dos bebidas a 6 tazas: 1 × 3 = 3 → 3:6; 2 × 2 = 4 → 4:6 Compara el jugo: 4 > 3

level1.stem: Bag A has 4 oranges for $2. Bag B has 6 oranges for $4. Which bag costs less for 1 orange?
level1.stemEs: La bolsa A tiene 4 naranjas por $2. La bolsa B tiene 6 naranjas por $4. ¿Qué bolsa cuesta menos por 1 naranja?
hints: Divide each cost by the number of oranges. The lower price wins.
hintsEs: Divide cada costo entre el número de naranjas. Gana el precio más bajo.
level1.explanation: Find each price for 1 orange: $2 ÷ 4 = $0.50; $4 ÷ 6 ≈ $0.67 Choose the lower price: $0.50 < $0.67
level1.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 naranja: $2 ÷ 4 = $0.50; $4 ÷ 6 ≈ $0.67 Elige el precio más bajo: $0.50 < $0.67

level1.stem: Pack A has 2 apples for $1. Pack B has 5 apples for $3. What is the lower price for 1 apple?
level1.stemEs: El paquete A tiene 2 manzanas por $1. El paquete B tiene 5 manzanas por $3. ¿Cuál es el precio más bajo por 1 manzana?
hints: Divide each cost by the number of apples. Then compare.
hintsEs: Divide cada costo entre el número de manzanas. Luego compara.
level1.explanation: Find each price for 1 apple: $1 ÷ 2 = $0.50; $3 ÷ 5 = $0.60 Choose the lower price: $0.50 < $0.60
level1.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 manzana: $1 ÷ 2 = $0.50; $3 ÷ 5 = $0.60 Elige el precio más bajo: $0.50 < $0.60

level1.stem: Chef Reyes uses 2 tablespoons of cocoa for 3 ounces of milk. Chef Tran uses 3 tablespoons for 5 ounces of milk. Scale both to 15 ounces of milk. Whose cocoa is more chocolatey?
level1.stemEs: El chef Reyes usa 2 cucharadas de cocoa por 3 onzas de leche. El chef Tran usa 3 cucharadas por 5 onzas de leche. Escala las dos a 15 onzas de leche. ¿Cuál cocoa es más chocolatosa?
hints: Multiply each recipe so the milk is 15 ounces. Then compare the cocoa.
hintsEs: Multiplica cada receta para que la leche sea 15 onzas. Luego compara la cocoa.
level1.explanation: Scale Chef Reyes's recipe by 5: 2 × 5 = 10 → 10:15 Scale Chef Tran's recipe by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 → 9:15 Compare the cocoa: 10 > 9
level1.explanationEs: Escala la receta del chef Reyes por 5: 2 × 5 = 10 → 10:15 Escala la receta del chef Tran por 3: 3 × 3 = 9 → 9:15 Compara la cocoa: 10 > 9

level2.stem: Box A has 10 granola bars for $4. Box B has 12 granola bars for $6. Which box is the better buy?
level2.stemEs: La caja A tiene 10 barras de granola por $4. La caja B tiene 12 barras de granola por $6. ¿Qué caja es la mejor compra?
hints: Find the price for 1 bar in each box.
hintsEs: Halla el precio de 1 barra en cada caja.
level2.explanation: Find each price for 1 bar: $4 ÷ 10 = $0.40; $6 ÷ 12 = $0.50 Choose the lower price: $0.40 < $0.50
level2.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 barra: $4 ÷ 10 = $0.40; $6 ÷ 12 = $0.50 Elige el precio más bajo: $0.40 < $0.50
choices: Box B — it has more bars
They cost the same per bar
choiceFeedback: $0.50 per bar is more than $0.40 per bar. The lower price for 1 bar wins.
More bars is not a fair test. Compare the price for 1 bar.
$4 ÷ 10 = $0.40 and $6 ÷ 12 = $0.50. They are not the same.

level2.stem: Drink A uses 3 scoops of powder for 5 cups of water. Drink B uses 5 scoops for 8 cups of water. Scale both to 40 cups of water. For 40 cups of water, how many scoops does the stronger drink use?
level2.stemEs: La bebida A usa 3 medidas de polvo por 5 tazas de agua. La bebida B usa 5 medidas por 8 tazas de agua. Escala las dos a 40 tazas de agua. Para 40 tazas de agua, ¿cuántas medidas usa la bebida más fuerte?
hints: Find each scale factor to 40. Then compare the scoops.
hintsEs: Halla cada factor de escala hasta 40. Luego compara las medidas.
level2.explanation: Scale Drink A by 8: 3 × 8 = 24 → 24:40 Scale Drink B by 5: 5 × 5 = 25 → 25:40 Pick the larger number of scoops: 25 > 24
level2.explanationEs: Escala la bebida A por 8: 3 × 8 = 24 → 24:40 Escala la bebida B por 5: 5 × 5 = 25 → 25:40 Elige el mayor número de medidas: 25 > 24

level2.stem: Store A sells 3 pens for $3.60. Store B sells 5 pens for $5.50. What is the lower price for 1 pen?
level2.stemEs: La tienda A vende 3 plumas por $3.60. La tienda B vende 5 plumas por $5.50. ¿Cuál es el precio más bajo por 1 pluma?
hints: Divide each cost by the number of pens. Then compare.
hintsEs: Divide cada costo entre el número de plumas. Luego compara.
level2.explanation: Find each price for 1 pen: $3.60 ÷ 3 = $1.20; $5.50 ÷ 5 = $1.10 Choose the lower price: $1.10 < $1.20
level2.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 pluma: $3.60 ÷ 3 = $1.20; $5.50 ÷ 5 = $1.10 Elige el precio más bajo: $1.10 < $1.20

level2.stem: Mix A uses 4 cups of juice for 10 cups of water. Mix B uses 6 cups of juice for ? cups of water. The two mixes taste the same. Find the missing number.
level2.stemEs: La mezcla A usa 4 tazas de jugo por 10 tazas de agua. La mezcla B usa 6 tazas de jugo por ? tazas de agua. Las dos mezclas saben igual. Halla el número que falta.
hints: Divide 4:10 by 2 first. Then scale it up to 6 cups of juice.
hintsEs: Primero divide 4:10 entre 2. Luego escálala hasta 6 tazas de jugo.
level2.explanation: Divide both numbers by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2; 10 ÷ 2 = 5 Multiply both numbers by 3: 2 × 3 = 6; 5 × 3 = 15
level2.explanationEs: Divide los dos números entre 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2; 10 ÷ 2 = 5 Multiplica los dos números por 3: 2 × 3 = 6; 5 × 3 = 15

level2.stem: Paint A mixes 1 cup of red with 2 cups of white. Paint B mixes 2 cups of red with 5 cups of white. Which paint is more red?
level2.stemEs: La pintura A mezcla 1 taza de rojo con 2 tazas de blanco. La pintura B mezcla 2 tazas de rojo con 5 tazas de blanco. ¿Qué pintura es más roja?
hints: Scale both mixes to 10 cups of white. Then compare the red.
hintsEs: Escala las dos mezclas a 10 tazas de blanco. Luego compara el rojo.
level2.explanation: Scale Paint A by 5: 1 × 5 = 5 → 5:10 Scale Paint B by 2: 2 × 2 = 4 → 4:10 Compare the red: 5 > 4
level2.explanationEs: Escala la pintura A por 5: 1 × 5 = 5 → 5:10 Escala la pintura B por 2: 2 × 2 = 4 → 4:10 Compara el rojo: 5 > 4

level3.stem: Car A travels 180 miles on 6 gallons. Car B travels 225 miles on 9 gallons. Which car gets better gas mileage?
choices: Car B, at 25 miles per gallon
Car B, because it traveled farther
Car A, at 30 miles per gallon
choiceFeedback: 25 miles per gallon is Car B's rate and it is computed correctly, but 30 is the larger rate.
Car B did travel farther, but it burned more gas doing it. Compare miles PER GALLON.
180 divided by 6 is 30 and 225 divided by 9 is 25, so the two rates differ.
level3.explanation: Car A: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 miles per gallon. Car B: 225 ÷ 9 = 25 miles per gallon. 30 > 25, so Car A gets better mileage.

level3.stem: Ty says the ratio 7:10 is greater than 3:4, because 7 > 3. Which statement is true?
level3.stemEs: Ty dice que la razón 7:10 es mayor que 3:4, porque 7 > 3. ¿Qué enunciado es verdadero?
hints: Make the second numbers the same. 20 works for 10 and 4.
hintsEs: Haz que los segundos números sean iguales. 20 sirve para 10 y 4.
level3.explanation: Scale 7:10 by 2: 7 × 2 = 14 → 14:20 Scale 3:4 by 5: 3 × 5 = 15 → 15:20 Compare the first numbers: 15 > 14
level3.explanationEs: Escala 7:10 por 2: 7 × 2 = 14 → 14:20 Escala 3:4 por 5: 3 × 5 = 15 → 15:20 Compara los primeros números: 15 > 14
choiceFeedback: That is Ty's mistake. With 20 as the second number, 7:10 is 14:20 and 3:4 is 15:20.
14:20 and 15:20 are not equal, so the ratios are not equal.

level3.stem: Tea A uses 2 spoons of honey for 9 cups of tea. Tea B uses 3 spoons of honey for 12 cups of tea. Which tea is sweeter?
level3.stemEs: El té A usa 2 cucharadas de miel por 9 tazas de té. El té B usa 3 cucharadas de miel por 12 tazas de té. ¿Qué té es más dulce?
hints: Find a common multiple of 9 and 12. Then compare the honey.
hintsEs: Halla un común múltiplo de 9 y 12. Luego compara la miel.
level3.explanation: Scale Tea A by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 → 8:36 Scale Tea B by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 → 9:36 Compare the honey: 9 > 8
level3.explanationEs: Escala el té A por 4: 2 × 4 = 8 → 8:36 Escala el té B por 3: 3 × 3 = 9 → 9:36 Compara la miel: 9 > 8

level3.stem: Bird A flies 54 miles in 3 hours. Bird B flies 75 miles in 5 hours. How many more miles per hour does the faster bird fly?
level3.stemEs: El ave A vuela 54 millas en 3 horas. El ave B vuela 75 millas en 5 horas. ¿Cuántas millas por hora más vuela el ave más rápida?
hints: Find the miles per hour for each bird. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Halla las millas por hora de cada ave. Luego resta.
level3.explanation: Find each unit rate: 54 ÷ 3 = 18; 75 ÷ 5 = 15 Subtract the unit rates: 18 − 15 = 3
level3.explanationEs: Halla cada tasa unitaria: 54 ÷ 3 = 18; 75 ÷ 5 = 15 Resta las tasas unitarias: 18 − 15 = 3

level3.stem: Shop A sells 6 pens for $4.50. Shop B sells 8 pens for $5.60. Shop C sells 10 pens for $7.20. What is the lowest price for 1 pen?
level3.stemEs: La tienda A vende 6 plumas por $4.50. La tienda B vende 8 plumas por $5.60. La tienda C vende 10 plumas por $7.20. ¿Cuál es el precio más bajo por 1 pluma?
hints: Find three unit prices. Then pick the lowest one.
hintsEs: Halla tres precios unitarios. Luego elige el más bajo.
level3.explanationEs: Halla cada precio por 1 pluma: $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75; $5.60 ÷ 8 = $0.70; $7.20 ÷ 10 = $0.72 Elige el precio más bajo: $0.70 < $0.72 < $0.75
